---
title: "About"
description: "Andy Chamberlin, research data scientist at Stanford: drone and satellite mapping, computer vision and spatial modeling for disease ecology and agriculture."
---

I'm a research data scientist at Stanford, working with the research groups of Giulio De Leo,
Joelle Rosser and Erin Mordecai on schistosomiasis, dengue and the landscapes behind them. On
most of these projects I'm the technical lead for the drone and remote sensing side.

## What I do

I work across the whole arc of a project:

- Shaping the questions and writing the grants
- Designing studies and planning drone missions
- Processing and calibrating drone and satellite imagery
- Building computer vision models that pull features out of that imagery
- Analysis and modeling
- Presentations and papers

## Methods

- **Imagery:** drone mapping, multispectral and spectral analysis, radiometric calibration,
  satellite imagery and Google Earth Engine
- **Terrain and water:** elevation models, hydrological modeling and flow routing
- **Computer vision:** deep learning to detect objects and map land cover, testing models in new
  places, scaling drone results up to satellite
- **Statistics:** spatial statistics, machine learning, Bayesian inference, species distribution
  models
- **Tools:** Python, R, QGIS, GPU model training on Stanford's computing cluster

## With others

None of this is solo work. It rests on the field teams, labs and partners in Senegal, Brazil,
Kenya, Indonesia and Costa Rica, and on the scientists who lead these projects.

## Background

- B.S., Biology, University of Wisconsin–Madison
- FAA Part 107 remote pilot; private pilot license
- Consultant to Conservation International, mapping water-management infrastructure in
  sub-Saharan Africa (2019–2020)
- French and Spanish
- Field photography and video
